A) A Cost Management Viewpoint
B) An Application Portfolio Rationalization Viewpoint (addressing the TIME model concern)
C) A Technology Standards Viewpoint
D) A Business Capability Viewpoint

Answer: B — The CFO's concern is application portfolio value and investment decisions. The Viewpoint that addresses this concern would specify: show applications by Business Value and Technical Health; classify as Tolerate/Invest/Migrate/Eliminate; show recommended actions. The resulting View is the TIME Model Portfolio Assessment. This is the Concern → Viewpoint → View chain applied to the CFO's specific question.

Q19. (Scenario) At the start of a new architecture initiative, an architect is asked to explain what the "Enterprise Continuum" is. She says: "It's the classification system we use to organize architecture assets — from the most generic ones that apply to any organization, all the way to the very specific architectures we develop for our own situation. When we start designing, we look at what generic or industry-specific architectures already exist and use them as starting points." Is she correct?

A) Partially correct — the Enterprise Continuum classifies only technology, not architecture
B) Incorrect — the Enterprise Continuum is the same as the Architecture Repository
C) Correct — the Enterprise Continuum is a classification system for organizing architecture and solution assets on a spectrum from generic (Foundation) to organization-specific, enabling reuse by starting from existing assets and customizing toward specific needs
D) Incorrect — the Enterprise Continuum only applies to reference architectures from external sources

Answer: C — The architect's description is accurate. Enterprise Continuum: classification scheme for architecture and solution assets, organized from Foundation (most generic) through Common Systems and Industry to Organization-Specific. The key principle: start from the most specific existing asset and customize it toward your organization's needs. This promotes reuse.

Q20. Which of the following BEST describes the purpose of the TOGAF III-RM (Integrated Information Infrastructure Reference Model)?

A) A checklist for assessing whether an organization's information infrastructure is compliant with international standards
B) A reference architecture showing how Business Applications, Infrastructure Applications, and the Application Platform interoperate to support seamless, "boundaryless" information flow across the enterprise
C) A model for organizing information systems into three tiers: presentation, business logic, and data
D) The TOGAF equivalent of the Zachman Framework's information row

Answer: B — III-RM: a specific architecture pattern (not a taxonomy or checklist) showing how three layers — Business Applications (specific to the organization), Infrastructure Applications (shared services like email, directory, security), and Application Platform (the middleware and platform services) — work together. The goal is "boundaryless information flow" — any authorized person can access any information they need, regardless of where it lives. This is distinct from the TRM (which is a taxonomy of service categories, not an architecture pattern).

Q21. (Scenario) An architecture team is reviewing ANDH's current state. They discover that patient appointment data is recorded by three different systems: the call center system (creates appointments), the hospital reception system (updates appointments), and the clinical portal (reads appointments and marks them as completed). They want to document which system Creates, Reads, Updates, and Deletes each data entity, and use this to determine data ownership. Which artifact captures this analysis?

A) Application Communication Diagram
B) Data Flow Diagram
C) Data Entity/Application Matrix (using CRUD notation)
D) Application/Organization Matrix

Answer: C — Data Entity/Application Matrix with CRUD notation: rows = data entities (Appointment), columns = applications (Call Center, Reception, Clinical Portal), cells = Create/Read/Update/Delete operations. The system that Creates (C) an entity is its owner. This matrix directly answers "which system owns which data" — the foundational question for MDM design and access control.

Q22. In TOGAF, the Architecture Board is described as having several responsibilities. Which of the following is NOT a responsibility of the Architecture Board?

A) Reviewing and approving architecture compliance assessments
B) Granting Dispensations for Non-conformant implementations
C) Designing the Target Architecture for each ADM cycle
D) Maintaining standards and governance processes for architecture

Answer: C — The Architecture Board GOVERNS architecture — it reviews, approves, arbitrates, and enforces. It does NOT design architecture. Architects and architecture teams design the architecture. The Architecture Board approves it. This is one of the most common exam traps: confusing the Board's governance role with the architect's design role.

Q23. (Scenario) ANDH is implementing its integration platform (WP-002). During Phase G, the implementation team discovers that the HL7 FHIR R4 API for the Pharmacy system will not be ready until 3 months after the planned integration platform go-live. The team proposes going live with the integration platform using a temporary HL7 v2 interface for Pharmacy, with a commitment to migrate to FHIR R4 within 3 months. The Architecture Contract requires HL7 FHIR R4 for all interfaces. What is the correct process?

A) The team can proceed without any formal approval — temporary workarounds are standard practice
B) This is a Non-conformant situation; the team should submit a Dispensation Request to the Architecture Review Committee, documenting the HL7 v2 temporary interface, the risk, and the 3-month migration commitment
C) Cancel the Pharmacy integration entirely until FHIR R4 is ready
D) Issue an Architecture Change Request to change the standard from FHIR R4 to HL7 v2 permanently

Answer: B — Dispensation Request: the implementation deviates from the Architecture Contract (HL7 FHIR R4 required, HL7 v2 proposed temporarily). This is a Non-conformant finding. The correct process is a Dispensation Request to the Architecture Review Committee — documenting the deviation, the reason (vendor readiness), the risk, and the time-bound remediation commitment (3 months). D would permanently change the architecture standard, which is inappropriate for a temporary technical constraint.

Q24. TOGAF describes Requirements Management as being at the center of the ADM wheel. Which statement MOST accurately captures why Requirements Management is represented this way?

A) Requirements Management is the most important phase and must be completed first
B) Requirements Management is a continuous process — not a phase — that simultaneously receives requirements from every ADM phase as they are discovered and feeds relevant requirements into every ADM phase as they proceed; it is the bidirectional hub connecting all phases
C) Requirements Management is performed only at the beginning (Phase A) and end (Phase F) of an ADM cycle
D) Requirements Management is where all stakeholder sign-offs are collected

Answer: B — Requirements Management is NOT a phase. It is a continuous, bidirectional process at the hub. It receives: new requirements discovered during B, C, D (e.g., "Phase C discovers a new data quality requirement not identified in Phase A"). It feeds: requirements into each phase as that phase needs them. The "wheel hub" representation captures this bidirectional, continuous nature — every phase connects to it.

Q25. (Scenario) An architect is explaining TOGAF to a new colleague who has a PRINCE2 background. The colleague asks: "How does a TOGAF Work Package relate to a PRINCE2 Project?" Which explanation is MOST accurate?

A) They are identical — Work Package and Project are TOGAF and PRINCE2 names for the same thing
B) A TOGAF Work Package is an architecture-level construct (from Phase E) defining WHAT needs to be done to close a set of architecture gaps. A PRINCE2 Project is the delivery vehicle for implementing that Work Package — it takes the Work Package specification and delivers it using project management disciplines.
C) A TOGAF Work Package is more detailed than a PRINCE2 Project — the Project is a high-level summary
D) Work Packages replace Projects in organizations that use TOGAF

Answer: B — Work Package (architecture level, Phase E): defines WHAT gap to close and its dependencies. PRINCE2 Project (delivery level): implements the Work Package using project management processes. Architecture Contract (Phase F) bridges them: it specifies what the Project must deliver and to what standard. The relationship: Work Package → Architecture Contract → PRINCE2 Project.

Q26. Which TOGAF Part is MOST directly responsible for providing guidance on how to adapt, abbreviate, combine, or iterate ADM phases to fit different organizational contexts?

A) Part I — Introduction
B) Part II — Architecture Development Method
C) Part III — ADM Guidelines and Techniques
D) Part VII — Architecture Capability Framework

Answer: C — Part III (ADM Guidelines and Techniques): explicitly provides guidance on HOW to adapt the ADM — iteration approaches, combining phases, abbreviating phases for Agile contexts, specific techniques (Business Scenarios, Risk Management, Capability-Based Planning, etc.). Part II contains the ADM itself (the phases). Part VII covers governance and the EA practice. Part I covers vocabulary.

Q27. (Scenario) An organization has just completed a major three-year digital transformation using TOGAF. The architecture is now deployed and operational. The EA team sets up monitoring processes to track: technology vendor announcements, regulatory changes, business strategy updates, and performance metrics from deployed systems. They receive change requests and evaluate each one. For minor optimizations that don't affect the architecture baseline, they implement changes directly. For significant changes affecting multiple domains, they prepare a new Phase E/F plan. For fundamental changes requiring complete redesign, they initiate a new Phase A. Which phase is the EA team operating in?

A) Phase F — Migration Planning
B) Phase G — Implementation Governance
C) Phase H — Architecture Change Management
D) Phase A — preparing for the next architecture cycle

Answer: C — Phase H (Architecture Change Management): monitors the deployed architecture, receives and evaluates change requests, and decides how to respond. The description maps exactly to Phase H's three change type responses: Simplification (minor → handle in Phase H), Incremental (significant multi-domain → Phase E/F), Re-architecting (fundamental → new Phase A). Phase G governs implementation of projects, not ongoing monitoring of deployed systems.

Q28. (Scenario) ANDH is using COBIT alongside TOGAF. The compliance team says: "We need to ensure that all architecture decisions are made within a proper governance framework that can be audited, that risk is formally accepted or mitigated, and that there is clear accountability for IT decisions." Which of the following BEST describes how TOGAF and COBIT complement each other in this context?

A) COBIT replaces TOGAF's governance elements — organizations should use COBIT governance, not TOGAF governance
B) TOGAF's Architecture Governance framework (Architecture Board, compliance assessments, dispensations) provides the architecture-specific governance; COBIT provides the broader IT governance and management controls and audit framework. The Architecture Board can be aligned with COBIT governance bodies, and Compliance Assessments can be aligned with COBIT control objectives.
C) They are competing frameworks and cannot be used simultaneously
D) TOGAF covers governance completely; COBIT is only needed for financial auditing

Answer: B — TOGAF and COBIT are complementary. TOGAF's Architecture Governance structures (Architecture Board, Compliance Assessments, ADRs) provide architecture-specific governance. COBIT provides the broader IT governance controls, risk management framework, and auditability structure. Organizations align them: Architecture Board maps to COBIT governance bodies; Dispensations are a form of COBIT risk acceptance; Compliance Assessments align with COBIT audit processes.

Q29. (Scenario) An architect is reviewing a proposed solution for a claims processing system. The solution uses the correct integration patterns, meets all performance requirements, uses all specified technology standards, and its architecture fully implements every aspect of the Architecture Contract without deviation. What compliance level applies?

A) Conformant
B) Fully Conformant
C) Compliant
D) Consistent

Answer: B — Fully Conformant: the solution fully implements the architecture in EVERY specified aspect with NO deviations. This is the strongest compliance level. Conformant allows for minor documented deviations (but this scenario has none). Compliant meets stated requirements without fully implementing all architecture aspects. The phrase "without deviation" is the key indicator for Fully Conformant.

Q30. An architect is deciding whether to use the TOGAF TRM or III-RM for a specific design task. She is designing the technology infrastructure for a new enterprise and needs to classify what types of technology services will be needed (database services, security services, messaging services, etc.). Which reference model is MOST appropriate for this task?

A) III-RM — because it shows how applications and infrastructure work together
B) TRM — because it provides a taxonomy of technology service categories that can be used to systematically identify and classify what technology is needed
C) Both equally — they serve the same purpose
D) Neither — the architect should design without reference models

Answer: B — TRM is the taxonomy of technology service categories — it is specifically designed for the task of "what types of technology do we need?" The architect uses the TRM category list (Data Management Services, Security Services, Network Services, etc.) to systematically ensure no service category is overlooked. The III-RM is used when the architect needs to design HOW these services integrate — it is an architecture pattern, not a taxonomy.

Q31. (Scenario) A Phase G Compliance Assessment finds that an e-commerce platform uses architecture vocabulary consistently with the target architecture (terms like "service," "API gateway," "event bus" are used correctly) but the platform was designed independently and has no direct relationship to the target architecture — it neither implements nor conflicts with it. The team says "we designed this ourselves, based on best practices, without referencing the architecture." Which compliance level applies?

A) Conformant
B) Compliant
C) Consistent
D) Irrelevant

Answer: C — Consistent: the solution uses the same terminology and concepts as the architecture but has no direct relationship to it — it neither conforms to it (actively implementing it) nor conflicts with it. "Uses the same language but has no direct relationship" = Consistent. This often occurs when teams adopt industry best practices that happen to align with terminology but didn't follow the architecture design process.

Q32. Which document in the TOGAF ADM formally defines how architecture compliance will be measured for an implementation project, specifying what must be built, what standards must be used, and what the acceptance criteria are?

A) Architecture Requirements Specification (ARS)
B) Statement of Architecture Work (SoAW)
C) Architecture Vision
D) Architecture Contract

Answer: D — Architecture Contract (Phase F): the governance agreement that specifies WHAT must be built, WHAT standards must be used, and HOW compliance will be measured (acceptance criteria). This is the document that Phase G Compliance Assessments are conducted against. The ARS contains requirements but is not a governance agreement. The SoAW governs architecture development. The Vision is aspirational.

Q33. (Scenario) An ANDH data architect needs to explain to the clinical team why establishing a Canonical Data Model (CDM) for clinical entities is important. Which explanation is MOST accurate?

A) "A CDM tells each system how to store its data internally"
B) "A CDM eliminates the need for any data transformations between systems"
C) "A CDM provides a single standardized format for data exchange — when systems need to share clinical data, they transform to and from this common format. This reduces the number of bilateral transformations from N×(N-1)/2 to N, making the integration landscape manageable."
D) "A CDM replaces Master Data Management — we only need one of the two"

Answer: C — CDM: a shared exchange format (NOT internal storage format — A is wrong). It reduces bilateral transformations to N (NOT eliminates all transformations — B is wrong). CDM addresses format incompatibility; MDM addresses authority (which system is authoritative) — they are complementary, not alternatives (D is wrong).

Q34. (Scenario) An architecture team applies the TOGAF ADM to a cloud migration project. They complete Phases A through D and now need to answer: "In what sequence should we migrate our 40 applications, and what intermediate operational states will we need to maintain during the migration?" Which ADM phase answers this question, and what are the key outputs?

A) Phase F — produces Architecture Contracts specifying migration sequence
B) Phase E — consolidates domain gap analyses, defines Work Packages (grouping applications by migration wave), defines Transition Architectures (the intermediate operational states), and produces Architecture Roadmap v0.1 and Implementation Plan v0.1
C) Phase G — governs the migration execution sequence
D) Phase H — manages the change during migration

Answer: B — Phase E: answers exactly "what sequence, and what intermediate states?" The Work Packages group related applications into migration waves. The Transition Architectures define each intermediate operational state (e.g., "State after Wave 1: applications 1-10 in cloud, 11-40 still on-premise, both must interoperate"). The Architecture Roadmap v0.1 shows the full sequence. This is Phase E's defining purpose.

Q35. A TOGAF architect is asked whether the Zachman Framework and TOGAF can be used together. Which statement MOST accurately reflects the recommended approach?

A) They cannot be used together — they are competing frameworks with conflicting assumptions
B) TOGAF should be used first to develop architecture; Zachman can then be used as a classification taxonomy to organize and categorize the artifacts that TOGAF's ADM produces
C) Zachman should be used first to classify requirements; TOGAF then implements them
D) Organizations must choose one; using both creates unnecessary complexity

Answer: B — TOGAF = process/method for developing architecture (ADM provides the development steps). Zachman = classification/ontology for organizing architecture artifacts (6×6 matrix provides the taxonomy). They are complementary: use TOGAF to do the EA work, use Zachman to organize and classify what you produce. This is the standard recommendation for organizations that want both a development method and a comprehensive artifact taxonomy.

Q36. (Scenario) ANDH has been in Phase H for 18 months. The EA team has received 47 change requests. Of these: 31 were minor optimizations handled within Phase H; 12 required looping back to Phase E/F for revised planning; 4 required initiating new Phase A cycles for complete redesign. Which Phase H change types do each of these numbers represent?

A) 31 = Simplification; 12 = Incremental; 4 = Re-architecting
B) 31 = Administrative; 12 = Tactical; 4 = Strategic
C) 31 = Minor; 12 = Medium; 4 = Major
D) All 47 are managed within Phase H — none require returning to other phases

Answer: A — Simplification Changes (31): minor, handled within Phase H, no ADM re-entry. Incremental Changes (12): moderate, require re-planning → loop to Phase E/F. Re-architecting Changes (4): fundamental → new Phase A cycle. Options B and C use non-TOGAF terminology. D is wrong — Incremental and Re-architecting changes DO require re-entry into earlier ADM phases.

Q37. (Scenario) A health technology company is evaluating two frameworks for data management alongside TOGAF. The CTO says: "We need a framework that defines WHO is responsible for data quality, WHAT processes manage data day-to-day, and HOW data governance is operationalized." The CDO says: "We need a framework that defines WHAT data entities we have, HOW data flows between systems, and WHAT the quality requirements are architecturally." Which framework answers each need?

A) CTO's need → TOGAF Phase C; CDO's need → DAMA-DMBOK
B) CTO's need → DAMA-DMBOK (Data Governance KA, Data Quality KA — operational management); CDO's need → TOGAF Phase C Data Architecture (data models, flows, quality requirements as architecture specifications)
C) Both needs are answered by TOGAF — DAMA-DMBOK is not relevant
D) Both needs are answered by DAMA-DMBOK — TOGAF is too high-level for data management

Answer: B — CTO's need = operational data management (WHO, WHAT processes, HOW governed) → DAMA-DMBOK. CDO's need = architectural data design (WHAT entities, HOW they flow, WHAT quality targets) → TOGAF Phase C. This is the TOGAF (architecture) vs. DAMA (management) distinction at its clearest. Both are needed.

Q38. Architecture Debt accumulates in organizations when:

A) The Architecture Board approves too many projects simultaneously
B) Dispensations are granted without remediation deadlines, implementations deviate from architecture without formal process, and planned migrations are deferred indefinitely — creating a growing gap between the approved architecture and the actual deployed state
C) Architecture Principles are too strict and cannot be followed in practice
D) Phase H is run too frequently, creating too many Architecture Change Requests

Answer: B — Architecture Debt: the accumulated deviation between the approved architecture and the actual deployed state. It grows through: dispensations never remediated (become permanent exceptions), informal deviations outside the governance process, deferred migrations (EOL systems still running), and undocumented workarounds. It is managed in Phase H and tracked in the debt register.

Q39. (Scenario) An architect presents the following business case to the ANDH Architecture Review Committee: "Our current Oracle 12c database platform was placed on the 'Retiring' standard list 18 months ago, requiring migration by end of Year 2. Several systems are still running on Oracle 12c. The vendor has now extended the EOL by 1 year. The project teams want to defer the migration by 1 year. Should we update the standard and defer the migration?" What is the correct TOGAF-aligned response?

A) Approve immediately — vendor extension justifies deferral
B) The Architecture Review Committee should formally evaluate this as an Architecture Change Request: assess the risks of continued Oracle 12c use (security posture, integration limitations), the cost savings of deferral, and whether deferring adds to Architecture Debt. Only approve if the risk assessment justifies it, and only with a firm new deadline.
C) Reject outright — Retiring standards cannot be changed
D) This is an operational decision, not an architecture governance matter

Answer: B — This is an Architecture Change Request (a change to an existing architecture standard). The ARC must formally evaluate it — not rubber-stamp it. Key considerations: What security risk does continued Oracle 12c use present? Does deferral add to Architecture Debt? Is the vendor extension actually a reason to defer, or does it just create false comfort? The ARC approves changes with governance, not informally. The change must include a revised, firm deadline.

Q40. (Scenario) An architect is reflecting on the ANDH scenario after completing Week 7. She notes: "Everything connects — the CEO's concern about business value (Phase A) drove the Business Capability gaps (Phase B), which drove the data entity requirements (Phase C Data), which drove the application rationalization (Phase C Application), which drove the cloud and HA decisions (Phase D), which all combined into the Work Packages and Transition Architectures (Phase E), which became Architecture Contracts (Phase F), which were enforced via compliance assessments (Phase G), and which are now being monitored and adapted (Phase H). And throughout all of this, the Architecture Repository stored everything — principles, architectures, standards, decisions, and governance records." What concept does this reflection best illustrate?

A) That TOGAF is overly complex and bureaucratic
B) That TOGAF's 7 parts form an integrated system — the ADM (Part II), Content Framework (Part IV), Enterprise Continuum (Part V), Reference Models (Part VI), Governance (Part VII), Techniques (Part III), and vocabulary (Part I) all work together as a coherent methodology for managing enterprise architecture
C) That all architecture work eventually ends in Phase H
D) That the Architecture Repository is the most important part of TOGAF

Answer: B — This is the integrated TOGAF system view — the synthesis understanding that separates candidates who can answer novel scenario questions from those who can only recall isolated facts. Each part of TOGAF serves a specific purpose, and they reinforce each other. The ADM is the process. Content Framework is what it produces. Enterprise Continuum is how it's classified. Repository is where it's stored. Governance is how it's controlled. The integrated view is what makes TOGAF work as a real methodology.
